title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome & parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia
presentation: Days after starting/escalating a dopamine antagonist (antipsychotics, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine), or after stopping/reducing dopaminergic drugs (parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia)
Fever, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability; evolves over days
definitions: Gurrera 2011 consensus elements: dopamine antagonist exposure or agonist withdrawal (recent); hyperthermia >38.0 °C on ≥2 occasions; rigidity; altered mental status; CK ≥4× ULN; sympathetic lability (BP ≥25% above baseline or fluctuation ≥20 mmHg diastolic / ≥25 mmHg systolic in 24 h; diaphoresis; incontinence); tachycardia ≥25% + tachypnea ≥50% above baseline; negative workup for other causes

Woodbury severity stages (Pileggi 2016, Table 3): I drug-induced parkinsonism; II drug-induced catatonia; III mild/early NMS (T <38 °C, HR ≤100); IV moderate (T 38–40 °C, HR 100–120); V severe (T ≥40 °C, HR ≥120)

immediateActions.action: Stop the dopamine antagonist even if the presentation is atypical; restart dopaminergic therapy as quickly as possible if it was withdrawn (NG if needed)
Supportive care: cooling blankets, IV fluids and electrolyte correction, VTE prophylaxis, aspiration precautions
ICU; add IV dantrolene to bromocriptine or amantadine

workup.test: Infection workup (blood cultures; LP if meningitis/encephalitis possible)
Medication review incl. antiemetics and recent parkinsonian drug changes

notes: Antipyretics are less effective than cooling (hyperthermia isn't prostaglandin-mediated)

treatment.doseText: Lorazepam 1–2 mg IM/IV q4–6h, or diazepam 10 mg IV q8h; taper
Severe NMS: 1–2.5 mg/kg (actual body weight) IV q6h or continuously for 48 h, then taper over several days
notes: Reulbach 2007 linked monotherapy with higher mortality, likely confounded by use in the most severe cases (Pileggi)

treatment.doseText: 2.5–5 mg PO/NG q8h; start low and titrate over several days; wean, don't stop abruptly
100 mg PO/NG q8h (moderate–severe; alternative to bromocriptine)
Restart prior carbidopa/levodopa regimen promptly; NG if NPO
notes: If no enteral route: rotigotine patch — dose it with the BMJ 2010 conversion on reference-cards:inpatient-parkinson-disease; don't use the calc:ledd (Jost) total as the input
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer (rotigotine as non-oral option; ungraded)

pitfalls: Atypical antipsychotics and antiemetics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) cause NMS too
NMS vs serotonin syndrome: NMS = slow onset, lead-pipe rigidity, bradyreflexia; SS = rapid onset, clonus, hyperreflexia
Abrupt levodopa stop (NPO, surgery) in Parkinson's can cause a NMS-like syndrome
Malignant catatonia overlaps — benzodiazepines help both
Rechallenge: wait ≥5 days (one series) to ≥14 days (another) after resolution; restart low and slow (Pileggi 2016)
escalateWhen: Temperature ≥40 °C, rising CK/renal failure, or autonomic instability → ICU
institutionVaries: Dantrolene stock location (often OR malignant-hyperthermia carts)
sources: Gurrera RJ, et al. An international consensus study of neuroleptic malignant syndrome diagnostic criteria using the Delphi method. J Clin Psychiatry 2011;72(9):1222-1228. doi:10.4088/JCP.10m06438
